name: Brown Sugar
lede: Brown Sugar is a warm reddish-orange brown named from a kitchen staple, one of hundreds of color names borrowed from food.

sections.title: A name from the kitchen
sections.body:
Brown Sugar is on the Wikipedia list of Crayola colors and in the 1930 Maerz and Paul dictionary, as cited in NBS Circular 553 of 1955 [1]. The swatch is a warm, muted reddish orange, nearest ISCC-NBS name "grayish reddish orange" at a distance of 5.0 [1]. Close neighbors include [[caramel]], [[tan]] and [[copper]].

Garfield reports Deane Judd's count of 7,500 color names, of which 239 came from foods, with brown sugar given as an example [2]. Jarman lists brown sugar among the homely brown things, with bread and eggs [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch appears in 882 of our 23,781 paintings, 3.71 percent, as photographed [4]. That is more common than 83 percent of named colors [4]. It peaks in the 1500s, found in 90 of the 2,231 paintings from that century, at 1.9 times the expected rate [4]. See [[brown]] and [[chocolate]] for the wider family.
